note: Sources of the files in this directory. Carl's session fetched them on 2026-11-06, outside every repository; this session copied them byte for byte (the sha256 of each is the one Carl's session recorded, and tests/multimessengerResults.test.js re-checks it). Only data, numbers and cited facts are recorded here; no text or table of a paper is reproduced, and the PDF, its extracted text, the FITS file and the saved policy pages stay outside the repository. Nothing in this directory was run as code.

leap-seconds.list.source: https://data.iana.org/time-zones/tzdb/leap-seconds.list (the IERS leap-second list as distributed with the IANA time zone database)
leap-seconds.list.terms: as read in the file itself: 'This file is in the public domain.'
leap-seconds.list.facts: last entry 3692217600 NTP seconds = 37 s from 1 January 2017; expiry line #@ 4023129600 (2027-06-28); update line #$ 3992312697

published-bound.json.source: Abbott et al. 2017 (LIGO Scientific Collaboration and Virgo Collaboration, Fermi GBM, INTEGRAL), ApJ 848, L13, arXiv:1710.05834; values transcribed as printed by Carl's session with a locator each
published-bound.json.terms: arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence, read on the abstract page on 2026-11-06 (the licence text itself was not saved); numbers and citation only
published-bound.json.note: the delay's free-text definition in this file reads the delay as a trigger against the GW time; the paper's own text defines the 1.74 s as the emission onset at geocenter (authentic-thresholds.json reading R1, and the supplement); the file is kept as supplied

published-bound-supplement.json.source: this session, from the same paper's extracted text by search, with a locator for each number
published-bound-supplement.json.terms: as published-bound.json: numbers and citation only

grb-trigger.json.source: NASA HEASARC Fermi GBM trigger archive, glg_tcat_all_bn170817529_v03.fit (primary header), https://heasarc.gsfc.nasa.gov/FTP/fermi/data/gbm/triggers/2017/bn170817529/current/glg_tcat_all_bn170817529_v03.fit
grb-trigger.json.terms: the Fermi Science Support Center data policy page (https://fermi.gsfc.nasa.gov/ssc/data/policy/) says that GBM data were not proprietary at any time during the mission and are released as early as possible; no licence text beyond that was found, and the NASA website disclaimer page states no data licence. Basis recorded as public archive data under that policy; only the trigger time and header keywords are kept here
grb-trigger.json.note: the header's TIMESYS is TT with MJDREF 51910 + 7.428703703703703D-4 (authentic-thresholds.json reading R3)
